speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for National Development with regard to keeping food prices affordable in the heartlands, whether the Ministry will consider taking further measures to assist stallholders of coffee shops who are facing increasing rentals and other business overheads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is part of HDB's effort to help operators and stallholders in a rising cost environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For sold eating houses, HDB does not regulate the stall rentals that owners charge as these transactions are private commercial agreements between the coffee shop owners and the stall operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Coffee shop operators and stallholders may tap on schemes, such as the Heartlands Go Digital Scheme, which supports enterprises in adopting digital solutions and improving their productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Business owners can visit the GoBusiness portal at gobusiness.gov.sg, for more information on the Government schemes available.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There have been reports of escalating rental prices, some as high as 20% to 30% in coffee shops, leading to stall holders giving up their businesses due to sustainability issues.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In keeping rentals affordable for essential heartlands food services, what are the considerations that the Ministry has in deciding which coffee shops are sold and which are rented from the HDB?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry also consider putting in place programmes with third-party owners or master operators of coffee shops to regulate rentals and business costs to keep food prices reasonable?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In response to Ms Yeo Wan Ling's supplementary question, HDB began selling HDB coffee shops in 1988, but ceased doing so from 1998 onwards.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, from 1998 onwards, we have not been selling coffee shops in HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Further, after a pilot in 2017, from 2018 onwards, we have been tendering out new HDB coffee shops using the Price Quality Method.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This would put weightage, not just on the rental bid; but, also on the coffee shop operators' ability to fulfil quality criteria.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also take the availability of affordable meals into consideration.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In the recent couple of years, we have also been implementing the Budget Meal initiative, which I believe Members of the House are quite familiar with.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is how we look at maintaining the availability of affordable food.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As a landlord, HDB plays its part by keeping rent stable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I have also explained that just now, in the main reply.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, we are mindful that the coffee shops need to be operated by people in the trade.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are also mindful that HDB is not, itself, directly in the business of cooked food provision.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, we do need to allow room for the coffee shop operators as well as stallholders, to abide by market principles and operate.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But we do our part to keep rents stable and also to encourage the provision of affordable meals via the Budget Meal initiative.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for the practices that Ms Yeo Wan Ling has mentioned, I would appreciate it if she could provide us with more details.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think Ms Yeo would appreciate that our approach towards sold privately-owned coffee shops would have to be different than the ones that HDB owns and then rents out, because the relationship with the operators in the two instances are quite different.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Nonetheless, I also believe that in Ms Yeo Wan Ling's ward, I think, all the coffee shops in the HDB estates in her ward are owned by HDB.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, we will continue to play our role as a responsible landlord.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And, if there are specific practices that she is aware of and, which she has concerns about, please raise it to us and we will study it carefully to see if intervention is warranted, particularly, if these coffee shops are owned by HDB.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Because, I think, just like the Member Ms Yeo, in my constituency of Sengkang, we have challenges with private operators, where, because they have increased their rent, it has also resulted in a pass-through to higher food prices for residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But since the Senior Minister of State has shared that since the 1990s, they no longer have this sale of coffee shop spaces to private operators, I wonder whether there are any plans afoot, or even intent, to potentially re-acquire some of these, so that the entire umbrella of coffee shops would be fully-owned by HDB?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, the Senior Minister of State said that it was 90%, if I recall correctly, or more than 90% that are already directly managed and owned by HDB.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And in terms of how the Government generally deals with the private sector, I think it is also important that we are clear about where the market is free to operate and where the Government comes in with interventions.
